sanskrit: paruṣāṇi sabhāmadhye proktavān yaḥ sma pāṇḍavān sa karṇo nirjitaḥ saṃkhye saindhavaś ca nipātitaḥ
english: That Karṇa who hurled harsh words at the Pāṇḍavas in the midst of the assembly hall has been worsted in battle, and the lord of the Sindhus laid low as well.

sanskrit: yasya vīryaṃ samāśritya śamaṃ yācantam acyutam tṛṇavat tam ahaṃ manye sa karṇo nirjito yudhi
english: That Karṇa, leaning on whose prowess I held the unfallen one who came seeking peace to be no more than a blade of grass — that very Karṇa has been beaten in the fight.

sanskrit: evaṃ klāntamanā rājann upāyād droṇam īkṣitum āgaskṛt sarvalokasya putras te bharatarṣabha
english: Thus crushed in spirit, O king, your son — he who has wronged the whole world — drew near to look upon Droṇa, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tat sarvam ācakhyau kurūṇāṃ vaiśasaṃ mahat parān vijayataś cāpi dhārtarāṣṭrān nimajjataḥ
english: Then he recounted the whole of it: the great slaughter of the Kurus, the foes carrying off the victory, and the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra going under.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca paśya mūrdhāvasiktānām ācārya kadanaṃ kṛtam kṛtvā pramukhataḥ śūraṃ bhīṣmaṃ mama pitāmaham
english: Duryodhana said: Behold, O teacher, the havoc wrought among the consecrated kings — though we set in the forefront the hero Bhīṣma, my grandsire.

sanskrit: taṃ nihatya pralubdho 'yaṃ śikhaṇḍī pūrṇamānasaḥ pāñcālaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvaiḥ senāgram abhikarṣati
english: Having struck him down, this Śikhaṇḍin, greedy and swollen with pride, together with all the Pāñcālas presses upon the van of our army.

sanskrit: aparaś cāpi durdharṣaḥ śiṣyas te savyasācinā akṣauhiṇīḥ sapta hatvā hato rājā jayadrathaḥ
english: And another, unassailable — your own pupil, the ambidextrous archer — after destroying seven full armies, has slain King Jayadratha.

sanskrit: asmadvijayakāmānāṃ suhṛdām upakāriṇām gantāsmi katham ānṛṇyaṃ gatānāṃ yamasādanam
english: How shall I ever discharge my debt to friends who longed for my victory and served my cause, now that they have gone to the abode of Yama?

sanskrit: ye madarthaṃ parīpsanti vasudhāṃ vasudhādhipāḥ te hitvā vasudhaiśvaryaṃ vasudhām adhiśerate
english: Those lords of the earth who sought to win the earth for my sake — they have forsaken dominion over the earth and now lie sleeping upon it.

sanskrit: so 'haṃ kāpuruṣaḥ kṛtvā mitrāṇāṃ kṣayam īdṛśam nāśvamedhasahasreṇa pātum ātmānam utsahe
english: I, a coward, having brought about such ruin of my friends — not by a thousand horse-sacrifices could I dare to redeem myself.

sanskrit: mama lubdhasya pāpasya tathā dharmāpacāyinaḥ vyāyacchanto jigīṣantaḥ prāptā vaivasvatakṣayam
english: For me — the greedy, the sinful, the transgressor of righteousness — they strove and sought to conquer, and so have come to the dwelling of Vaivasvata.

sanskrit: kathaṃ patitavṛttasya pṛthivī suhṛdāṃ druhaḥ vivaraṃ nāśakad dātuṃ mama pārthivasaṃsadi
english: How is it that the earth could not open a cleft to swallow me — fallen in conduct, betrayer of my own friends — there in the assembly of kings?

sanskrit: so 'haṃ rudhirasiktāṅgaṃ rājñāṃ madhye pitāmaham śayānaṃ nāśakaṃ trātuṃ bhīṣmam āyodhane hatam
english: I could not save my grandsire, his limbs drenched in blood, lying in the midst of the kings — Bhīṣma struck down upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: taṃ mām anāryapuruṣaṃ mitradruham adhārmikam kiṃ sa vakṣyati durdharṣaḥ sametya paralokajit
english: When that unassailable conqueror of the world beyond meets me — ignoble man, betrayer of friends, doer of unrighteousness — what will he say to me?

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ paśya sātyakinā hatam madartham udyataṃ śūraṃ prāṇāṃs tyaktvā mahāratham
english: Behold the mighty archer Jalasaṃdha, slain by Sātyaki — a hero who rose up for my sake and gave his life, a great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: kāmbojaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā tathālambusam eva ca anyān bahūṃś ca suhṛdo jīvitārtho 'dya ko mama
english: Seeing the Kāmboja struck down, and Alambusa too, and many other friends besides — what use to me now is the wish to live?

sanskrit: vyāyacchanto hatāḥ śūrā madarthe ye 'parāṅmukhāḥ yatamānāḥ paraṃ śaktyā vijetum ahitān mama
english: The heroes who, never turning their backs, exerted themselves and fell for my sake, striving with all their might to conquer my enemies —

sanskrit: teṣāṃ gatvāham ānṛṇyam adya śaktyā paraṃtapa tarpayiṣyāmi tān eva jalena yamunām anu
english: to them, O scorcher of foes, I shall this day discharge my debt as best I can: I shall offer them the water of libation along the Yamunā.

sanskrit: satyaṃ te pratijānāmi sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ vara iṣṭāpūrtena ca śape vīryeṇa ca sutair api
english: Truly I vow it to you, O foremost of all who bear arms — I swear it by my sacrifices and pious works, by my valor, and by my sons —

sanskrit: nihatya tān raṇe sarvān pāñcālān pāṇḍavaiḥ saha śāntiṃ labdhāsmi teṣāṃ vā raṇe gantā salokatām
english: having slain in battle all those Pāñcālas together with the Pāṇḍavas, I shall win peace — or else I shall go to share their world in the fight.

sanskrit: na hīdānīṃ sahāyā me parīpsanty anupaskṛtāḥ śreyo hi pāṇḍūn manyante na tathāsmān mahābhuja
english: For now my allies, ill requited, no longer desire to aid me; they reckon the sons of Pāṇḍu worthier than us, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: svayaṃ hi mṛtyur vihitaḥ satyasaṃdhena saṃyuge bhavān upekṣāṃ kurute suśiṣyatvād dhanaṃjaye
english: Death itself has been ordained in battle by him whose vows are truth; yet you show indifference toward Dhanaṃjaya, because he is so apt a pupil.

sanskrit: ato vinihatāḥ sarve ye 'smajjayacikīrṣavaḥ karṇam eva tu paśyāmi saṃpraty asmajjayaiṣiṇam
english: And so all who wished to make me victorious have been struck down; in Karṇa alone do I now see one who still seeks my triumph.

sanskrit: yo hi mitram avijñāya yāthātathyena mandadhīḥ mitrārthe yojayaty enaṃ tasya so 'rtho 'vasīdati
english: The dull-witted man who, not truly knowing his friend, yet employs him in a friend's behalf — his purpose comes to nothing.

sanskrit: tādṛgrūpam idaṃ kāryaṃ kṛtaṃ mama suhṛdbruvaiḥ mohāl lubdhasya pāpasya jihmācārais tatas tataḥ
english: Such has been this enterprise of mine, contrived out of folly by those who only call themselves friends — by their crooked dealings, here and there, against a greedy and sinful man.

sanskrit: hato jayadrathaś caiva saumadattiś ca vīryavān abhīṣāhāḥ śūrasenāḥ śibayo 'tha vasātayaḥ
english: Slain is Jayadratha, and the valiant son of Somadatta, and the Abhīṣāhas, the Śūrasenas, the Śibis, and the Vasātis.

sanskrit: so 'ham adya gamiṣyāmi yatra te puruṣarṣabhāḥ hatā madarthaṃ saṃgrāme yudhyamānāḥ kirīṭinā
english: This very day I too shall go where those bulls among men have gone — slain for my sake in battle as they fought against the diademed one.

sanskrit: na hi me jīvitenārthas tān ṛte puruṣarṣabhān ācāryaḥ pāṇḍuputrāṇām anujānātu no bhavān
english: For I have no use for life bereft of those bulls among men. Let the teacher of the sons of Pāṇḍu grant me his leave to go.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca sindhurāje hate tāta samare savyasācinā tathaiva bhūriśravasi kim āsīd vo manas tadā
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When the king of the Sindhus had been slain in battle by the ambidextrous archer, dear son, and Bhūriśravas likewise, what then was the temper of your minds?

sanskrit: duryodhanena ca droṇas tathoktaḥ kurusaṃsadi kim uktavān paraṃ tasmāt tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: And Droṇa, thus addressed by Duryodhana in the assembly of the Kurus — what did he say in reply to that? Tell me this, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca niṣṭānako mahān āsīt sainyānāṃ tava bhārata saindhavaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūriśravasam eva ca
english: Saṃjaya said: A great clamor of dismay arose among your troops, O Bhārata, when they beheld the lord of the Sindhus slain and Bhūriśravas as well.

sanskrit: mantritaṃ tava putrasya te sarvam avamenire yena mantreṇa nihatāḥ śataśaḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: They all scorned the whole of your son's counsel — that counsel by which warriors among the kṣatriyas had been slain by the hundred.

sanskrit: droṇas tu tad vacaḥ śrutvā putrasya tava durmanāḥ muhūrtam iva tu dhyātvā bhṛśam ārto 'bhyabhāṣata
english: But Droṇa, hearing those words of your son, grew downcast in spirit; and after pondering a moment, sorely afflicted, he spoke.

sanskrit: duryodhana kim evaṃ māṃ vākśarair abhikṛntasi ajayyaṃ samare nityaṃ bruvāṇaṃ savyasācinam
english: O Duryodhana, why do you thus pierce me with the shafts of your words, when I have ever told you the ambidextrous archer is unconquerable in battle?

sanskrit: etenaivārjunaṃ jñātum alaṃ kaurava saṃyuge yac chikhaṇḍy avadhīd bhīṣmaṃ pālyamānaḥ kirīṭinā
english: By this alone, O Kaurava, you might have understood Arjuna in war — that Śikhaṇḍin slew Bhīṣma while guarded by the diademed one.

sanskrit: avadhyaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃyuge devamānuṣaiḥ tadaivājñāsiṣam ahaṃ neyam astīti bhāratī
english: When I saw one whom neither gods nor men could slay struck down in battle, even then I knew: this host of ours shall be no more.

sanskrit: yaṃ puṃsāṃ triṣu lokeṣu sarvaśūram amaṃsmahi tasmin vinihate śūre kiṃ śeṣaṃ paryupāsmahe
english: When that hero is slain whom we held the bravest of men in all three worlds, what remnant do we still cling to?

sanskrit: yān sma tān glahate tātaḥ śakuniḥ kurusaṃsadi akṣān na te 'kṣā niśitā bāṇās te śatrutāpanāḥ
english: Those dice which father Śakuni cast in the assembly of the Kurus — they were no dice but whetted arrows, tormentors of the foe.

sanskrit: ta ete ghnanti nas tāta viśikhā jayacoditāḥ yāṃs tadā khyāpyamānāṃs tvaṃ vidureṇa na budhyase
english: Those very shafts, dear son, now slay us, driven on toward our undoing — the shafts of which Vidura warned you then, though you would not understand.

sanskrit: tās tā vilapataś cāpi vidurasya mahātmanaḥ dhīrasya vāco nāśrauṣīḥ kṣemāya vadataḥ śivāḥ
english: You would not heed those words of the great-souled, steadfast Vidura, though he cried them out for your welfare — auspicious counsel spoken for your good.

sanskrit: tad idaṃ vartate ghoram āgataṃ vaiśasaṃ mahat tasyāvamānād vākyasya duryodhana kṛte tava
english: And now this dreadful thing is come to pass, this great slaughter — through your scorning of that counsel, Duryodhana, for your sake.

sanskrit: yac ca naḥ prekṣamāṇānāṃ kṛṣṇām ānāyayaḥ sabhām anarhatīṃ kule jātāṃ sarvadharmānucāriṇīm
english: And in that you had Kṛṣṇā dragged before the assembly while we looked on — she undeserving of it, nobly born, a follower of every sacred duty —

sanskrit: tasyādharmasya gāndhāre phalaṃ prāptam idaṃ tvayā no cet pāpaṃ pare loke tvam arcchethās tato 'dhikam
english: of that unrighteousness, O son of Gāndhārī, you have now received the fruit; and were it not so, you would meet a sin still greater in the world beyond.

sanskrit: yac ca tān pāṇḍavān dyūte viṣameṇa vijitya ha prāvrājayas tadāraṇye rauravājinavāsasaḥ
english: And in that you conquered the Pāṇḍavas at dice by foul play and drove them then into the forest, clad in the skins of black antelopes —

sanskrit: putrāṇām iva caiteṣāṃ dharmam ācaratāṃ sadā druhyet ko nu naro loke mad anyo brāhmaṇabruvaḥ
english: toward these men, who walk ever in righteousness as though they were my own sons — what man in the world, save me who am called a brāhmaṇa, would deal so treacherously?

sanskrit: pāṇḍavānām ayaṃ kopas tvayā śakuninā saha āhṛto dhṛtarāṣṭrasya saṃmate kurusaṃsadi
english: This wrath of the Pāṇḍavas was brought down by you together with Śakuni, with Dhṛtarāṣṭra's assent, in the assembly of the Kurus.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanena saṃyuktaḥ karṇena parivardhitaḥ kṣattur vākyam anādṛtya tvayābhyastaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Joined to it was Duḥśāsana, and Karṇa nourished it the more; and you, disregarding the steward's words, fed it again and again.

sanskrit: yat tat sarve parābhūya paryavārayatārjunim sindhurājānam āśritya sa vo madhye kathaṃ hataḥ
english: When all of you, overpowering Abhimanyu, hemmed him round while rallying about the king of the Sindhus — how then was that king slain in your very midst?

sanskrit: kathaṃ tvayi ca karṇe ca kṛpe śalye ca jīvati aśvatthāmni ca kauravya nidhanaṃ saindhavo 'gamat
english: How, while you and Karṇa and Kṛpa and Śalya yet lived, and Aśvatthāman too, O Kaurava, did the lord of the Sindhus go to his death?

sanskrit: yad vas tat sarvarājānas tejas tigmam upāsate sindhurājaṃ paritrātuṃ sa vo madhye kathaṃ hataḥ
english: When all those kings of yours waited upon his fierce splendor to save the lord of the Sindhus — how was he slain in your very midst?

sanskrit: mayy eva hi viśeṣeṇa tathā duryodhana tvayi āśaṃsata paritrāṇam arjunāt sa mahīpatiḥ
english: On me above all, O Duryodhana, and on you, that lord of earth set his hope of deliverance from Arjuna.

sanskrit: tatas tasmin paritrāṇam alabdhavati phalgunāt na kiṃ cid anupaśyāmi jīvitatrāṇam ātmanaḥ
english: And now, since he found no rescue from Phalguna, I see no way at all to save my own life.

sanskrit: majjantam iva cātmānaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnasya kilbiṣe paśyāmy ahatvā pāñcālān saha tena śikhaṇḍinā
english: I see myself, as it were, sinking into the guilt that is Dhṛṣṭadyumna, so long as I have not slain the Pāñcālas together with that Śikhaṇḍin.

sanskrit: tan mā kim abhitapyantaṃ vākśarair abhikṛntasi aśaktaḥ sindhurājasya bhūtvā trāṇāya bhārata
english: Why then do you pierce me with the shafts of your words while I burn with grief, O Bhārata, when you yourself were powerless to save the king of the Sindhus?

sanskrit: sauvarṇaṃ satyasaṃdhasya dhvajam akliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ apaśyan yudhi bhīṣmasya katham āśaṃsase jayam
english: You did not see, in battle, the golden banner of Bhīṣma, the tireless-handed one whose word was truth — how then do you still hope for victory?

sanskrit: madhye mahārathānāṃ ca yatrāhanyata saindhavaḥ hato bhūriśravāś caiva kiṃ śeṣaṃ tatra manyase
english: Where, in the midst of mighty chariot-warriors, the lord of the Sindhus was slain, and Bhūriśravas too — what remnant do you suppose is left there?

sanskrit: kṛpa eva ca durdharṣo yadi jīvati pārthiva yo nāgāt sindhurājasya vartma taṃ pūjayāmy aham
english: If the unassailable Kṛpa yet lives, O king — he who has not gone the road of the lord of the Sindhus — him I honor.

sanskrit: yac cāpaśyaṃ hataṃ bhīṣmaṃ paśyatas te 'nujasya vai duḥśāsanasya kauravya kurvāṇaṃ karma duṣkaram avadhyakalpaṃ saṃgrāme devair api savāsavaiḥ
english: And in that I saw Bhīṣma slain before the very eyes of your younger brother Duḥśāsana, O Kaurava — Bhīṣma, who wrought deeds so hard to do, well-nigh unslayable in battle even by the gods with Vāsava at their head —

sanskrit: na te vasuṃdharāstīti tad ahaṃ cintaye nṛpa imāni pāṇḍavānāṃ ca sṛñjayānāṃ ca bhārata anīkāny ādravante māṃ sahitāny adya māriṣa
english: this I now think, O king: that the earth is no longer yours. For here, O Bhārata, the hosts of the Pāṇḍavas and the Sṛñjayas, joined together, are charging upon me this day, honored sir.

sanskrit: nāhatvā sarvapāñcālān kavacasya vimokṣaṇam kartāsmi samare karma dhārtarāṣṭra hitaṃ tava
english: Not until I have slain all the Pāñcālas will I loose my armor; in battle, O son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, I shall do the deed that serves your good.

sanskrit: rājan brūyāḥ sutaṃ me tvam aśvatthāmānam āhave na somakāḥ pramoktavyā jīvitaṃ parirakṣatā
english: O king, say to my son Aśvatthāman in the fray: the Somakas must not be spared by one who would guard his own life.

sanskrit: yac ca pitrānuśiṣṭo 'si tad vacaḥ paripālaya ānṛśaṃsye dame satye ārjave ca sthiro bhava
english: And keep faith with the counsel your father gave you: stand firm in mercy, in self-restraint, in truth, and in uprightness.

sanskrit: dharmārthakāmakuśalo dharmārthāv apy apīḍayan dharmapradhānaḥ kāryāṇi kuryāś ceti punaḥ punaḥ
english: Skilled in duty, gain, and pleasure, never letting duty or gain suffer harm, holding duty foremost — so should you perform your tasks, again and again.

sanskrit: cakṣurmanobhyāṃ saṃtoṣyā viprāḥ sevyāś ca śaktitaḥ na caiṣāṃ vipriyaṃ kāryaṃ te hi vahniśikhopamāḥ
english: The brāhmaṇas are to be gratified with eye and mind, and served according to one's power; nothing should be done to displease them, for they are like tongues of fire.

sanskrit: eṣa tv aham anīkāni praviśāmy arisūdana raṇāya mahate rājaṃs tvayā vākśalyapīḍitaḥ
english: But now I plunge into the hostile ranks, O slayer of foes, for a great battle, O king — wounded as I am by the barb of your words.

sanskrit: tvaṃ ca duryodhana balaṃ yadi śaknoṣi dhāraya rātrāv api hi yotsyante saṃrabdhāḥ kurusṛñjayāḥ
english: And you, Duryodhana, hold the army together if you can; for even by night the Kurus and Sṛñjayas, roused to fury, will fight on.

sanskrit: evam uktvā tataḥ prāyād droṇaḥ pāṇḍavasṛñjayān muṣṇan kṣatriyatejāṃsi nakṣatrāṇām ivāṃśumān
english: So saying, Droṇa went forth against the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas, stealing away the splendor of the warriors as the sun steals the light of the stars.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tato duryodhano rājā droṇenaivaṃ pracoditaḥ amarṣavaśam āpanno yuddhāyaiva mano dadhe
english: Saṃjaya said: Then King Duryodhana, so goaded by Droṇa, fell into the grip of indignation and set his mind on battle alone.

sanskrit: abravīc ca tadā karṇaṃ putro duryodhanas tava paśya kṛṣṇasahāyena pāṇḍavena kirīṭinā ācāryavihitaṃ vyūhaṃ bhinnaṃ devaiḥ sudurbhidam
english: And then your son Duryodhana said to Karṇa: Behold — the battle-array drawn up by the teacher, hard for the very gods to break, has been broken by the diademed son of Pāṇḍu with Kṛṣṇa for his ally.

sanskrit: tava vyāyacchamānasya droṇasya ca mahātmanaḥ miṣatāṃ yodhamukhyānāṃ saindhavo vinipātitaḥ
english: While you exerted yourself, and the great-souled Droṇa too, and the foremost of warriors looked on, the lord of the Sindhus was struck down.

sanskrit: paśya rādheya rājānaḥ pṛthivyāṃ pravarā yudhi pārthenaikena nihatāḥ siṃhenevetarā mṛgāḥ
english: Behold, O son of Rādhā, the kings, the foremost upon earth in war, slain by Pārtha alone, as lesser beasts are slain by a lion.

sanskrit: mama vyāyacchamānasya samare śatrusūdana alpāvaśeṣaṃ sainyaṃ me kṛtaṃ śakrātmajena ha
english: Though I strove in the battle, O slayer of foes, my army has been brought to a scant remnant by the son of Śakra.

sanskrit: kathaṃ hy anicchamānasya droṇasya yudhi phalgunaḥ bhindyāt sudurbhidaṃ vyūhaṃ yatamāno 'pi saṃyuge
english: For how, if Droṇa had not willed it, could Phalguna in battle have broken that array so hard to break, however he might have striven in the fray?

sanskrit: priyo hi phalguno nityam ācāryasya mahātmanaḥ tato 'sya dattavān dvāraṃ nayuddhenārimardana
english: For Phalguna is ever dear to the great-souled teacher; and so, O crusher of foes, he granted him passage without a fight.

sanskrit: abhayaṃ saindhavasyājau dattvā droṇaḥ paraṃtapaḥ prādāt kirīṭine dvāraṃ paśya nirguṇatāṃ mama
english: Droṇa, scorcher of foes, having granted safety to the lord of the Sindhus in the fight, yet opened the gate for the diademed one — behold how poorly I am served.

sanskrit: yady adāsyam anujñāṃ vai pūrvam eva gṛhān prati sindhurājasya samare nābhaviṣyaj janakṣayaḥ
english: Had I but given leave at the outset for the king of the Sindhus to go home, there would have been no slaughter of men in the battle.

sanskrit: jayadratho jīvitārthī gacchamāno gṛhān prati mayānāryeṇa saṃruddho droṇāt prāpyābhayaṃ raṇe
english: Jayadratha, longing for life, was setting out toward home, having won safety from Droṇa in the fight — and I, ignoble, held him back.

sanskrit: adya me bhrātaraḥ kṣīṇāś citrasenādayo yudhi bhīmasenaṃ samāsādya paśyatāṃ no durātmanām
english: This day my brothers, Citrasena and the rest, are spent in battle, having come up against Bhīmasena before our wicked-hearted eyes.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca ācāryaṃ mā vigarhasva śaktyā yudhyaty asau dvijaḥ ajayyān pāṇḍavān manye droṇenāstravidā mṛdhe
english: Karṇa said: Do not reproach the teacher; that brāhmaṇa fights with all his might. I deem the Pāṇḍavas unconquerable in the fray, even by Droṇa who knows every weapon.

sanskrit: tathā hy enam atikramya praviṣṭaḥ śvetavāhanaḥ daivadṛṣṭo 'nyathābhāvo na manye vidyate kva cit
english: For even so, passing him by, the white-horsed one broke through. The course of things is ordained by fate; I think there is nowhere any altering it.
